_doc: Intel Archive (generated by gravelight/tools_src/extract_intel.py from docs/gravelight/LORE.md section 13). placement fixed = a hand-placed StoryProp (data/gravelight/story_props.json), never in the random spawn; placement companion = filed when Jakub joins (U02 section 6.2), never spawned.

intel.title: The Innkeeper's Notebook (Anselm Vogt)
intel.text: "The radio picks up the mine again tonight. Not music, a man reading numbers in English. My wife says it's the English spies. I think it's the mine itself."

intel.title: Frequency Card (Blue)
intel.text: A torn card reading "3.120 — the doctor." The innkeeper's handwriting. One of the three radio quest notes.

intel.title: Frequency Card (Grey)
intel.text: "5.785 — never after midnight." The back has a child's drawing of a drummer.

intel.title: Frequency Card (Red)
intel.text: "7.440 — if the bell rings, turn it off."

intel.title: Flight Log, GRAVELIGHT ONE
intel.text: Selwyn's last entry: "23:41. Violet light, bearing 040. Both engines out. Instruments dead. Watches stopped. Gliding. God bless."

intel.title: Photograph: Kreuzweg, 1937
intel.text: The inn in summer, a family in the doorway. On the back, three names and "Wilcza Góra wedding."

intel.title: Road Garrison Orders, 21 Dec
intel.text: "All personnel will avoid the Kaltenbrunn road. Do not engage persons coming from the mine. Repeat: do not let them touch you."

intel.title: Glasmacher Transmission (fragment)
intel.text: "…the light was not your fault and not your pilot's. It was ours. It was mine, I think. Follow the rails."

intel.title: Fasbender: "On Sustained Impulse" (1940)
intel.text: The first page of the Nachhall-Hypothese paper. A margin note in Reinholt's hand: "Emil — if it can sustain a step, can it sustain a word?"

intel.title: Reinholt Cylinder #1: "Why"
intel.text: "They ask why a physiologist wants a mine. I tell them: for the Fatherland. I am lying. I want my daughter's laugh. Everything else is paperwork."

intel.title: Reinholt Cylinder #4: "One Hundred and Eighty-Seven"
intel.text: "One hundred and eighty-seven. The Obersteiger says they were 'unproductive units.' I record them as a number because if I record them as men I will stop."

intel.title: Reinholt Cylinder #9: "Herr Tamtam"
intel.text: "I put a piece of her in his drum. Foolish. She always said he was lonely on the shelf." (The EE step 7 foreshadow.)

intel.title: Helvetia Automaten AG: Contract Extract
intel.text: "…12 (twelve) hygienic dispensers, enamel finish, sponsor livery at buyer's discretion, coin mechanism to accept facility tokens…" Signed K. Imhof.

intel.title: Helvetia Advertising Proof: Ironhide Stout
intel.text: A full-color ad proof: the riveted barrel mascot flexing. "Iron in the Barrel, Iron in the Man!"

intel.title: Kessler's Brewing Log
intel.text: "The formula tastes of tin and graves. I have added roasted barley, molasses, and spite. The engineers ask for seconds. God forgive me, it's good stout."

intel.title: Infirmary Ledger: Sister A. W.
intel.text: Dosage tables in Polish, disguised as laundry counts. One line: "T.N. — 4471 — two drops, will live."

intel.title: Opitz: Notes on the PA Voice
intel.text: "Fed the Hauptbuch the Marchbank reels. It reads the tally beautifully. Today it said 'good morning' to me. I did not program 'good morning.'"

intel.title: Ledger Tape: Unscheduled Broadcast, 21 Dec
intel.text: The Operator, to an empty facility: "Good evening, everyone. Tonight's tally: four thousand and eleven. Tremendous. Is anyone listening? Do say if you are."

intel.title: Mahlknecht's Shift Book
intel.text: "Gallery 7. Haze rising. Bell rung. Gates locked per my order to protect the lift. 187 units remain inside. Production unaffected."

intel.title: Photograph: The Salt Chapel, 1912
intel.text: Miners in their Sunday best under the new bell, with a priest blessing it. Written on the frame: "Dzwon na zmianę" ("a bell for the shift").

intel.title: Bell Protocol (Resonance Alarm)
intel.text: "On hearing the bell, all gallery personnel will cease work and walk to the chapel with lamps lit. Do not run. Do not stop."

intel.title: Fasbender: Personal Note
intel.text: "The aircraft must come close enough. If the pulse is timed, they cannot turn back." No date. Unsigned, but in his hand.

intel.title: Fasbender to Reinholt (unsent)
intel.text: "Augusta, it is not her. It is the stone remembering a shape. Please. If you love her, let her be quiet."

intel.title: Photograph: Liesl with Herr Tamtam
intel.text: A girl in a paper hat marching with a tin drummer, Berlin 1938. Written on the back: "Generalin Liesl inspects the troops."

intel.title: Death Certificate: Liesl Reinholt
intel.text: Charité hospital, 9 February 1939. Cause: diphtheria. Reinholt has underlined "antitoxin administered day 4" three times.

intel.title: Stimmversuch Report: Schw. Brandauer
intel.text: "Subject continues to sing. Subject's voice now registers on the resonance gauges. Subject's voice is carried by the stone. Subject is no longer breathing."

intel.title: Lenz Duty Roster, 20 December
intel.text: Forty names, all crossed out in different inks. The last, Lenz, crossed out in violet pencil.

intel.title: Laborer's Letter (Polish)
intel.text: "Mamo, they feed us a little better since the nurse came. We sing on Sundays in the salt church. Tomek sings loudest." (Tomek is Tomasz.)

intel.title: Abteilung III: Tonic Field Trial Summary
intel.text: "Eleven deaths among long-term users. All eleven reanimated within six hours, regardless of cause of death. Recommend: do not inform the troops."

intel.title: Operator Calibration Reel
intel.text: The Operator cycling voices: Marchbank's, then a telephonist's, then a girl's: "one… two… tam…" Then it laughs. Opitz never built a laugh.

intel.title: Opitz: Totenglocke Sketch
intel.text: A handheld bronze bell-cannon. "If a bell can quiet them, a small bell can quiet them nearer. Will not build. Do not tell the doctor."

intel.title: Nursery Inventory
intel.text: "1 cot, white. 1 rocking horse. Wallpaper (ducks). 1 tin drummer — MISSING since 22 Dec. Search the crates."

intel.title: Reinholt Cylinder #12: "The Twentieth"
intel.text: "I turned it to full. Something said Mama. I am sure of it. I am sure of it. And then the garrison started screaming."

intel.title: The Second Ledger (R. Fenske, Lohnbuchhalter)
intel.text:
A clothbound pay ledger wrapped in oilcloth, kept under a lifted board of the pay office floor; the pencil is still tied to it with string. Columns in a bookkeeper's hand, ruled with a ruler. Translated.

LABOURERS' PAY WITHHELD, KALTENBRUNN. Opened 3 March 1941. Closed: not closed.
One line per man, per week, to the pfennig. 3.III.41, Gallery Two crew, 41 men, nine weeks: RM 4,428.30. 10.III.41, same crew: RM 492.00. 17.III.41, same crew: RM 492.00. The totals run to the foot of the sixth page, across to the seventh, and over.
Nobody ordered this book. The Ledger has a column for the marked and no column for these men, so I made one. I do not know who will read it. I know the figure is correct. It is the only thing in this building that is.
Somebody should pay it one day. Not the Provider. Somebody.
(Beneath, in the same pencil, a short stroke at every thousand, as on the wall behind the counter.) R. FENSKE

intel.title: SOE Briefing Extract: GRAVELIGHT
intel.text: "Primary: extract GLASMACHER. Secondary: obtain material sample." Then a later, retyped version with the order of the two lines swapped.

intel.title: Directive LANTERN (partial)
intel.text: A heavily redacted page, initialed "H." Only these words survive: "…sample… at any cost… not to be shared with US personnel…" (Unlocks only after Peg's dossier level 5.)

intel.title: Letter: Deacon to Ruthie
intel.text: "Tell Mama I'm fine and the food's terrible. Tell Pop I've been fixing machines that don't deserve fixing. I'm going to fix them anyhow, then I'm going to break them proper."

intel.title: Postcard: Wilcza Góra, 1890
intel.text: A village church beside a pit headframe. On the back in Polish: "For Halinka, who is going across the sea." Dutch's grandmother.

intel.title: The Kreuzweg Guest Book
intel.text:
The inn's guest book, open on the bar at its last written page. Leather boards, ruled columns, the landlord's careful hand. Translated.

3.III.44. A. Gähwiler, carter, Basel. 1 night. Lorry in the yard. Load: 1 crate marked "Kühlanlage" (cooling plant), for the works. Knocked on the doorframe going in, and again coming out.
3.III.44. V. Vendelin, engineer, Basel. Room paid for, not used. Sat up all night by the stove in his coat and gloves. Ordered the soup. Did not eat it. Paid for it twice.
28.XI.44. Signals section, six men, quartered in the taproom by order. Their wireless set on my bar.
17.XII.44. Two gentlemen from the works, Rooms 2 and 3, three nights, billed to the Amt. Their escort, a lance-corporal, on the settle.
20.XII.44. The gentlemen recalled by telephone at 16:00. "Every hand for the doctor." Luggage left behind. In Room 3, a letter on the bed, no stamp. A.V.
21.XII.44. Signals section to the Kaltenbrunn road, on orders. Not back. Soup kept warm.
22.XII.44. No guests. Road shut. Käthe will not come away from the wireless.

The last line is in a child's pencil, pressed hard into the page: "Heute Nacht kommen vier Gäste vom Himmel. Zimmer machen! Das Mädchen im Radio sagt es." (Four guests are coming tonight, from the sky. Make up the rooms! The girl in the radio says so.)

intel.title: Wireless Log, Signals Section
intel.text:
A signals section's wireless log, left on the table by their kit crates. Pencil, two hands. Translated.

19.12. 21:30. Unlisted station on 5.785 again, from the direction of the works. A man reading numbers in English. Logged as enemy propaganda. The sergeant says it is a gramophone.
20.12. 23:02. Every band at once: one carrier, no voice, a hum under it. The set is warm in the hands with the battery out. The taproom lamps burn violet, then go out.
20.12. 23:09. Signal ends. Every watch in the section has stopped at 23:02.
21.12. 06:10. The English announcer on 5.785 wishes us "a very good evening, on this fine twentieth of December." It is the twenty-first.
21.12. 06:40. Orders by runner: section to the Kaltenbrunn road. Set left on the landlord's bar on listening watch. His girl promises not to touch it.

Below, in the landlord's hand: "22.12. They have not come back. After midnight the set talks to itself. A child sings on it, and Käthe sings back. A.V."

intel.title: Käthe's Drawing
intel.text:
Wax crayon on the back of a brewery order form, pinned at a child's height at the top of the stairs.

A wireless set drawn as big as a house. Inside it, a girl in a paper hat beats a drum. Behind her the crayon is violet, pressed so hard it has gone through the paper. Outside the set, a smaller girl with yellow plaits holds up a candle.

In careful capitals: "DAS MÄDCHEN IM RADIO. SIE SINGT WENN PAPA SCHLÄFT. SIE WILL ZU IHRER MAMA." (The girl in the radio. She sings when Papa is asleep. She wants her mama.)

Along the bottom edge, a row of drumbeats: tam-tam, ta-ta-tam.

intel.title: Unsent Letter, Room 3
intel.text:
A letter left on the bed in Room 3, with an envelope addressed to Frau Hedwig Brenner, Liegnitz. No stamp. Translated.

Kreuzweg, 19 December 1944.
Dear Hedi, the Amt has given us three nights at a coaching inn nine kilometres from the works, which is their idea of Christmas. There is a fire, a landlord who keeps out of politics, and real coffee. Don't ask.
I sleep badly. The hum follows me even here. Nine kilometres, and I still feel it in my back teeth, like a train that never arrives.
I only wire relays, Hedi. I wire them and they count. Herr Opitz talks to them the way my father talked to horses, and lately I think they answer him.
At supper the landlord's little girl asked me if I work with the girl who sings. I told her there are no girls down there. She looked at me as if I had lied, and I think perhaps I had.
They will call us back early. Something is planned for the twentieth, and the doctor wants every hand. When it is over I am coming home, and I will never count anything again.
Your Josef

intel.title: Helvetia Delivery Docket
intel.text:
A printed delivery docket, filled in by hand and nailed to the cellar pillar where a carter would see it. Translated.

HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG. BASEL. SINCE 1921. Delivery docket No. 44/1187.
Consignee: Amt für Sonderforschung, Kaltenbrunn, Abt. III. Deliver to: Gasthaus Zum Kreuzweg, cellar (interim storage).
Goods: 8 (eight) hygienic beverage dispensers, enamel finish, sponsor livery. Replacement units, to be held until called for.
Coin mechanisms: facility tokens only. Tally line to the works: see Herr Opitz.
Delivered 9.X.44. Driver: A. Gähwiler. Fitted and tested: V. Vendelin, Ing.
Storage paid monthly to A. Vogt, in Reichsmark.

Pencil at the foot, in the landlord's hand: "They hum when the cellar is dark. My wife will not fetch the potatoes any more. A.V."
Below it, very small and very neat: "Cabinet 2: please do not disconnect. V."

intel.title: Framed Clipping: "A Hundred Years at the Crossroads"
intel.text:
A yellowed newspaper column behind glass over the taproom benches, from the district paper, summer 1936. Translated.

A HUNDRED YEARS AT THE CROSSROADS. The Gasthaus Zum Kreuzweg, last stop for the Kaltenbrunn salt carters, marks its centenary this month. Landlord Anselm Vogt tells our reporter that the mine's new deep galleries will bring the miners back, "and the beer will be waiting."

Tucked into the corner of the frame is a smaller cutting from November 1938: "KALTENBRUNN: BODIES TAKEN FROM MINE MORTUARY. Police suspect thieves. The two miners, Jan Pilch and Bruno Hasse, died on Friday of gas in a deep gallery."

Pencil in the margin: "Bruno sat at the corner table on Tuesday and drank to the new gallery. The milk girl from Wilcza Góra saw him that night on the salt road, walking back toward the mine. A.V."

intel.title: Infirmary Letter, Totenhafen
intel.text:
A letter in a nurse's hand, folded twice and left on the blanket of the end cot in the cannery's infirmary. Polish, with a German translation pencilled underneath by someone else. Translated.

Totenhafen, 4 January 1945.
To whoever is sent after us. They brought us up from Kaltenbrunn on the ore train, eleven of the laborers and me, to nurse what was left of them in this fish hall. Six are still alive. The sixth is not the boy I pulled out of Gallery Seven; I looked.
The crates came down the line with us. Lead, sealed, cold to the touch in a warm room, the doctor's own marks on every one. The sailors will not go near them, and the officer calls them ballast and laughs.
Tonight they are taking the crates down to the pens, and I am ordered down with them, to "attend the cargo." I do not know what attending a crate means. I have left my cross in the stove. If you are reading this, the stove is cold.
Tell Zofia Nowak, if she is alive, that I kept my promise as far as the water. A. W.

intel.title: Pump-Room Log
intel.text:
The pump keeper's day book, swollen with damp, open on the desk beside the Pumpenschalter. Entries in a seaman's capitals; the last one in a different pencil. Translated.

5.I. 03:10. High water 2.2 under the deck. Both pumps running. Cargo on the apron, 14 units, lead, under tarpaulin. Nobody to sleep in the pens tonight, by order.
5.I. 05:40. U-1047 loading. The crates go in by the forward hatch, not the torpedo hatch. The nurse goes aboard with them. She is the only one who will touch them. The second watch refused and was marched up.
5.I. 06:55. Boat sailed on the morning ebb. Orders say she is for the south-west and a Swiss consignee. Orders say a great many things.
6.I. 03:20. High water. Pumps stopped by order, to save the fuel. The water came up to the deck and did not go out again on the ebb. Something walks on the apron at night that is not the watch. The watch is in the cannery with the doors chained.
(In the other pencil:) The pumps are not for the water.

intel.title: Loading Manifest, U-1047
intel.text:
A typed loading manifest nailed to the crane office's wall, the paper stiff with salt. Kriegsmarine letterhead over a Swiss company's shipping stamp. Translated.

LOADING MANIFEST. Boat: U-1047. Berth: Pen 2, Totenhafen. Sailing: 5.I.45, morning ebb.
Cargo: 14 (fourteen) ballast units, lead, sealed, 410 kg each. Origin: Kaltenbrunn, Abt. III (Dr. A. Reinholt). Stowage: forward, in place of reloads; trim to be corrected by the engineer.
Forwarding agent: HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG, Basel. Consignee: HALE, L., care of the agent. Delivery: as directed by the consignee at the rendezvous. Payment: settled in advance, per the agent.
Passenger: 1 (one) medical attendant, civilian, for the cargo. Not to be landed.
Remarks: the units are not to be opened at sea. The units are not to be stowed within 3 m of the crew's berths. In the event of loss, the agent is to be informed before the Flotilla.
(Stamped:) HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG. BASEL. SEIT 1921. KONTINUITÄT.

intel.title: Teletype Strip, Signal Room
intel.text:
A strip of teletype paper, metres of it, pinned to the signal room's wall where it spilled out of the machine. The port's own call sign at the head; after that, nothing the port ever sent. The German parts are translated; the rest came through in English.

TOTENHAFEN SIGNALS TO ALL STATIONS. EVENING TALLY. EVENING TALLY.
UNCLE LIONEL AND LIESL PRESENT THE EVENING TALLY. FOURTEEN UNITS OUTBOUND. SIX UNITS RETAINED IN THE CANNERY. ONE UNIT WALKING.
MAMA SAYS THE SEA IS A BIG RADIO. MAMA SAYS COUNT THE BOATS.
HIGH WATER AT THREE. HIGH WATER AT SIX. HIGH WATER AT NINE. DO STAY FOR THE WEATHER.
THANK YOU FOR YOUR CONTINUED ENGAGEMENT.
(The machine typed the last line four hundred times. The ribbon ran out halfway; the rest is pressed into the paper, blank.)

intel.title: Jakub's Letter to Marta (written in the coal cage)
intel.text:
Marto, moja kochana (Marta, my dear),

I am writing this with a pencil the length of my thumbnail, on the back of a coal bill, in a cage in the cellar of the Kreuzweg, where we used to sell Anselm his winter coal. Do not laugh. I know you are laughing.

I am out of Kaltenbrunn. On the night of the twentieth the bell rang and did not stop, and the guards ran from something they would not name. We went up the old Maintenance Stairs, eleven of us, the way we planned it in the spring. The guards on the third landing were still shooting. I was slow, because of my knee, and slow is careful, and careful is alive. I am sorry to tell you I was the only one who reached the snow. I said their names at the top, and I will say them to you at our table, every one.

I took a coat off the guardroom hook. It is too big and it smells of a stranger, and I cut the badges off with a shovel. On the road a patrol caught me and brought me here, and then they heard something on the road behind them and ran, and took the key with them.

Something is walking about upstairs. I am not afraid. I was under that mountain almost four years and it did not keep me. Tell Hania her father is coming home. Tell her to set the extra plate at Wigilia, for the stranger at the door. This year, God willing, the stranger is me.

Your Jakub.

P.S. The chalk is still on the props in Gallery Nine. Three strokes and a hook. If anyone ever asks you what it meant, tell them: we did not build their mountain well.

intel.title: The Engine Ledger (Werk Thalbach, file 1)
intel.text: "4 × impeller, Nachtglas type. Consignee: Werk Thalbach. Supplier: V. Valve plates in a script nobody in the drawing office could read. Fitted 2 May. They do not take fuel. The fitters asked what they take. The answer was: delivery."

intel.title: The Flight Plan (file 2)
intel.text: "Thalbach, 03:40. Climb to altitude over the North Sea. Westbound, the Atlantic. Sampling run along the eastern seaboard. Then the last waypoint: a dry lake in a desert nobody here can place on a map, in a hand nobody here has. Asked who wrote it. Nobody wrote it."

intel.title: The Crew List (file 3)
intel.text: "Der Kranich, crew for the long-distance flight. Pilot: PROVIDED. Flight engineer: Riedl, A. Gunners: PROVIDED. Navigator: PROVIDED. Below, in Wittkamp's hand: 'Provided by whom?' and below that, stamped: HANDLED."

intel.title: Jette Maurer's Logbook (the wind tunnel)
intel.text: "Rhön, 1934: a thermal off the Wasserkuppe held me for an hour and I came down where I meant to. That is the whole art: coming down where you meant to. ... Tunnel run 212, the Kranich at 1:20. She flies. She flies beautifully. ... Weight for the long flight, with the load: 61 400 kg. Asked to confirm the crew's dose of the ELEVATION substrate. Nein."

intel.title: Three Crew Tags (der Kranich)
intel.text: "RIEDL, A. — HAAS, W. — POHL, K. Stamped tin, the works' crane-in-a-cog, a serial each. Found in a buckled harness, on the tape deck, under a gunner's seat. The men were not aboard. The tags were."

intel.title: The Kranich's crew, on the racks
intel.text:
Three rack tags from the fulfillment store, matched to the three harness tags from the Kranich's blisters.

RIEDL, A. · Bordmechaniker · provided 2.V.45 · re-deployed RR-7 by fold, 9.V.45 · rack 2, bay 4.
HAAS, W. · Bordschütze · provided 2.V.45 · re-deployed RR-7, 9.V.45 · rack 2, bay 5.
POHL, K. · Bordschütze · provided 2.V.45 · re-deployed RR-7, 9.V.45 · rack 2, bay 6.

"Provided" is the crew list's word. The works' fitters wrote "CREW: PROVIDED" and did not ask by whom. The answer is on the tags, in the Provider's stamp: they were inventory before they were crew. Someone has scratched three strokes and a hook into every one of the three.

intel.title: The relay's model plate: RR-7 · MONDLICHT
intel.text:
REGIONAL RETENTION RELAY RR-7 · "MONDLICHT"
Field units 3 and 4, 1938–39. Crater floor, near side, one kilometre from the anomaly.

PURPOSE. To hold the regional Plan in force where the customer is unable to attend: the relay repeats the retention signal at the Earth without interruption. EXCEPTIONAL RETENTION.

INVENTORY. Reception dome (landing pad, airlock). Concourse (model, forge unit 001, cabinets 2–3). Fulfillment store (racks, fold pad, conveyor). Retention hall (columns I–III, the sign). The Account (console, the first retained, one executive unit, attending remotely).

NOTE, in a later hand: the forge has never been lit. The cabinets have never been filled. The model's little Earth is painted the wrong colour. Nobody has been here since the field units left, and the relay has not noticed.

intel.title: The first retained: a tag, and a theft report from 1938
intel.text:
TAG, stamped: PILCH, J. · KB · 11.XI.38.

Attached, a carbon of a report from the Kaltenbrunn mortuary shed, 12 November 1938: "One body removed overnight from shed 2. Pilch, Jan, 41, of the valley, killed in the salt on the 11th by a fall of roof. The shed was locked. The lock is undamaged. The night watchman reports a violet light at the shed window at about 03:00 and a sound he describes as 'a shop bell'. The family have been told he ran off. Recommend no further action."

Under the carbon, in the field units' hand: "Retained. Impulse: clean. Repeating at the Earth from 14.XI.38. Signal reach at first light: the valley. By spring: the district."

He has been under this glass for seven years. His hand still moves.

intel.title: A photograph of the crack, annotated "customer-generated"
intel.text:
A print, 9 by 12, taken from the crater rim toward the anomaly, dated April 1945 in the field units' hand. A smile-shaped crack in the regolith, a kilometre long, the violet light inside it over-exposed to white.

On the back: "The anomaly predates the relay. The relay was sited for it. It answers the signal; it did not originate it. Classification: customer-generated. No action."

A second note, pencil, a different hand, recent: "It blinked back at the men on the range in Nevada. It blinks at the Account Manager too. She does not like it. Nobody here is the customer. — D.M."

intel.title: Consignment Manifest, Crate D/LANTERN
intel.text:
A shipping manifest in a celluloid sleeve, tacked to the lid of a crate stencilled with a diamond and the word LANTERN. Typed, two carbons, a signature in ink.

CONSIGNMENT: one (1) crate, sealed, 212 lb. CONTENTS: specimen, geological, with fittings. ORIGIN: Totenhafen (occupied), by the hand of the retrieving officer. ROUTED: London, Admiralty annexe, for onward carriage. CONSIGNOR: Lt. M. Ashworth, R.N.V.R. (W). CONSIGNEE: Mr. L. Hale, Groom Lake range, Nevada, U.S.A. Priority: DIRECTIVE LANTERN. Retrieve at any cost.

Under the typed lines, pencil, an American hand: "Rec'd 14 April. Signed for by Mr. Hale personally. Opened in the lab 6 May. Nobody told the sergeant."

intel.title: Program Log, Mr. L. Hale
intel.text:
A bound program log on the office sill, open where it can be read through the glass. A civilian hand, exact and unhurried.

11 Aug 1944. Bolide over the range, 02:10. Impact on the dry lake, a crater the size of a motor car. Logged with the Weather Bureau as a meteor. It is not a meteor. It hums. The stone is in the lab pit by 15 Aug.

3 Sep. The dish pointed at the stone at the sergeant's suggestion (she wanted the tower's generator for her lights). The stone answers the dish. Direction of the reply: 0.5 degrees off the Moon's limb, the dark side of the crack. Nine months of listening since. It answers.

14 Apr 1945. The British crate. The second specimen is the same material. The two speak to each other through the floor.

6 May. The crate opened in the pit. Major Rourke insisted on standing closest. I have written to his wife. The program is not stopped; the program is why the rocket exists. Something on the Moon talks back, and I would like to know what, before anyone else does.

The last line, in a different pen: "The sergeant says I asked the Canaries nice. I did. I always do."

intel.title: Notice of Cancellation
intel.text:
A single sheet from the relay's console, printed on the Provider's own form, the one nobody printed. Across the top, in a hand that is not a machine's: KÜNDIGUNG. Below it, four signatures, and a fifth line left blank for whoever reads this next.

The Provider's note, stamped under the signatures: "Not a cancellation. The account is on extended leave." Someone has crossed out "extended leave" and written: cancelled.

intel.title: Implant Order 14/42 (Abteilung III)
intel.text:
A carbon of a typed order from Abteilung III, filed in the Admin Block, the stamp smudged violet at one edge. Translated.

AMT FÜR SONDERFORSCHUNG · KALTENBRUNN · ABT. III (FORMULIERUNG). Order 14/42, 14 June 1942. Subject: the Marke.
1. From Heart offcuts (lot H-7) the workshop will cut tokens of three by one and a half millimetres, polished, no facets. Yield per kilogram: Venner's sheet.
2. Implantation by the infirmary, under the skin of the right hand between thumb and forefinger, or of the forehead above the right brow where the hand is unsuitable (gloves, burns). Local anaesthetic. No cut over two millimetres.
3. Each token is read at the pay office and at the dispensers; pay, rations and facility tokens are tallied against it. The Hauptbuch carries the list.
4. Issue to: garrison, Abteilung staff, volunteers. Not to be issued to the labour contingents.
5. Wording for the men: die Marke, die dich hält. The mark that keeps you. Venner.

Under point 4, in a different ink and a careful hand: Nor offered. Those are not accounts. The initial is F.

intel.title: Recruiting Poster: "DIE MARKE, DIE DICH HÄLT"
intel.text:
A printed recruiting poster on the taproom's south wall, pasted over an older bill for the summer fair, one corner curling. A soldier's right hand held up, open, with a small violet point between thumb and forefinger drawn like a star. Translated.

DIE MARKE, DIE DICH HÄLT. The mark that keeps you.
Men of the district! The works at Kaltenbrunn take on guards, drivers, kitchen and store staff. Good pay, paid against the mark. Rations against the mark. Credit at the dispensers against the mark. One small token under the skin of the hand, and the works know you by name wherever you stand. You will never be lost to us.
Report to the pay office, Administration Block, Kaltenbrunn, Monday to Saturday. Volunteers of the Kreuzweg district: the carter calls Tuesdays.

Beneath, in pencil, the landlord's hand: The carters say they count you going in. I have not seen them count anyone coming out.

intel.title: Surgeon's Notes, Totenhafen Infirmary
intel.text:
A Kriegsmarine surgeon's notebook, left open on the middle cot of the cannery infirmary, the pages stiff with salt and something darker. The hand is steady until the last page. Translated.

6 January. Rating Behrens, U-1047's boat party, brought in from the apron with a crushed chest. Dead at 03:40. Marked, right hand, as they all are now. I removed the token through a two-millimetre cut, for the report they keep asking for, and put it in a saucer on the instrument table.
It was warm. I set that down because I will not believe it tomorrow.
03:52. The token is pulsing in the saucer. Not glowing: pulsing, like a thing with a heart, in time with the hum in the floor. Behrens is on the cot. Behrens's hand is opening and closing. Behrens has no pulse. I have checked three times.
04:10. I moved the saucer to the far end of the room. The hand slowed. I brought it back. The hand quickened. God forgive me, I did it twice.
04:30. He sat up. I have locked the door. I write this so that whoever comes after me knows: it is not the man that wants to get up. It is the thing in the hand, and it does not need the man.
Whoever reads this: do not take it out of them. Taking it out does not stop it. Stop the hum.

intel.title: Terms of the Mark (the Provider's form)
intel.text:
A single printed sheet on the reception desk under the bell, on the Provider's own form: a violet rule, the slogan in the corner. The one thing on the Moon that reads like a contract. Nobody has signed it.

TERMS OF THE MARK. Regional edition, Sol-3.
1. THE MARK. A retention token of substrate, chip-sized, placed at the customer's right hand or brow. The mark is the account. The account is the customer.
2. TERM. The Plan runs for the customer's life and continues thereafter without interruption, renewal or notice. Death is not a cancellation event.
3. SERVICE. For the duration of the term the customer's last engagement is sustained by the regional carrier (Earth) and the Regional Retention Relay (RR-7). Where the carrier is interrupted, service pauses; the Provider does not warrant the customer's condition during a pause.
4. CONSIDERATION. Pay, rations and loyalty points are tallied against the mark by the Provider's regional engine. Points do not expire. Customers do not expire.
5. TRANSFER. The mark may not be removed, sold or assigned. Removal does not end the Plan.
6. CANCELLATION. See 2.
7. RETENTION. Exceptional.

At the foot, a field for the customer's name, left blank. Beside it, in a later hand: Nobody read it. That was the product.

intel.title: Jakub's Refusal (chalk, Gallery Nine, transcribed)
intel.text:
A timber prop's worth of chalk, copied in pencil onto a sheet and pinned to the wall of the Maintenance Stairs' second landing, where the men who planned the climb could read it. The marks are the labourers' prop alphabet; the transcription is in Polish and German under each line. Translated.

Three strokes and a hook, twice: weak, ours, don't trust it. Then, in the long form the timbermen used for a message meant for someone who was not there yet:

They came down to Nine with the box and the needle and asked the gang leaders first. They said: a mark in the hand, and you are known by name, and your pay is against it and your bread is against it. They said: the mark that keeps you.
I said: I have a name. It is enough to carry. I said: you held our pay in March of forty-one and our ration cards against our wives, and now you offer me a thing to hold them against. No.
They wrote something by my number and went up. Nobody in Nine took it. Nobody in Nine was asked twice.
To whoever reads this after me: whatever they keep with that mark, they keep. Do not let them keep you.
J.O., May 1943.

Beneath, in a second chalk, a hook drawn backwards.

intel.title: A Rating's Letter, Never Sent
intel.text:
A letter folded small and pushed into a tobacco tin, found on the quay where the cutter lay before it slipped into the sea. The envelope is addressed to Glückstadt and was never stamped. Translated.

Totenhafen, 18 January 1945.
Dear Mother,
We are still in the pen. They do not tell us when we sail and the Old Man does not tell them either, which you would like, he is from the coast like us. The cargo is aboard and nobody sleeps forward. Brecht says it is only lead. Brecht does not sleep forward either.
Yesterday they lined up the whole detachment on the apron and a doctor from the Abteilung went down the line with a little gun, like the one the vet uses on the cattle, and put a grain into the back of each man's right hand, between the thumb and the finger. "Die Marke, die dich hält," he said every time. It stings, and then it is cold, and then it is nothing. Heinz says it is for the pay and the rations. I do not think it is for the pay.
Give Lotte my love and tell her I kept the drawing she sent. Tell her the sun in it is the only sun we have seen this month.
Your son, Jens.

intel.title: Telegram from Basel
intel.text:
A telegram form torn off the signal room's teletype and left in its tray, the strip pasted down in two lines the way the post office does it. Translated from the German routing; the message came through in English.

BASEL 19 1 45 0310 FOR KPTLT LENZ U 1047 TOTENHAFEN = SAIL ON THE NEXT TIDE OR THE DETACHMENT IS RETAINED =
= HALE L PER HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG STOP NO REPLY REQUIRED =

intel.title: Cannery Pay Slip
intel.text:
A pay slip from the cannery office's desk, printed on cheap grey card, the figures filled in by a clerk with a blunt pencil. Translated.

FISCHKONSERVENFABRIK TOTENHAFEN. Wage account, week 2/1945.
Worker: no. 0417, line II (gutting). Hours: 71.
Wage: 71 h at the Ledger rate . . . 42 Scrip.
Less: canteen 11 Scrip. Less: lodging 9 Scrip. Less: contribution to the Ledger 14 Scrip. Less: breakages (one knife) 3 Scrip.
To pay: 5 Scrip. Redeemable at the works canteen only.
(Stamped:) PAID IN FULL. THANK YOU FOR YOUR CONTINUED ENGAGEMENT.
(Pencilled underneath, in another hand:) and they wonder why we stopped singing on the line

intel.title: A Child's Drawing
intel.text: A child's crayon drawing of a grey boat on blue water under a large yellow sun with a smiling face, pinned beside the shelter door at child height; on the back, in careful letters, "Papas Boot".

intel.title: Hinnerk Petersen's Ration Book
intel.text:
A civilian ration book on the signal room's chart table, the cover soft with salt, most of its coupons torn out. Name: Petersen, Hinnerk. Occupation: harbour pilot. The back pages are full of pencil. Translated.

Bread: 3 coupons left. Fat: none. Tobacco: traded for paraffin.
(Pencil, inside the back cover:) HW 06.12 / 18.40. Springs on the 20th. Do not take her out on the springs.
14 lead boxes went down to the apron on the ore train. The Kapitänleutnant asked me how deep it is past the breakwater. I told him the truth. He wrote it down.
The lighthouse keeper has not answered the lamp since Tuesday.
If anybody reads this, I am up the tower. The stairs flood. Bring a gun.

intel.title: Field units 3 and 4: the delivery log, RR-7
intel.text:
DELIVERY LOG · FIELD UNITS 3 & 4 · RR-7 "MONDLICHT"

1938-11. Relay hull, sections A to F. Signed for: unit 3.
1939-02. Forge unit 001 (uncrated, not lit). Signed for: unit 4.
1939-04. Racks, three. Hangers, twenty-seven. Signed for: unit 3.
1939-06. Retention columns I-III. Sign, NOBODY CANCELS, letters 13. Signed for: unit 4.
1939-08. Executive unit (remote attendance). Signed for: nobody. Signed for itself.
1945-05. Inventory, Kranich, three (RIEDL, HAAS, POHL). Racked, bay 4-6. Signed for: unit 3.

The last column, every entry: DELIVERED BEFORE YOU ASKED.
Units 3 and 4 still walk the rim. They do not come in. Their lamps are on a timer.

intel.title: A tag on a hanger: rack 2, bay 5
intel.text:
HAAS, K.
BORDSCHUETZE
PROVIDED 2.V.45
RR-7 · RACK 2 · BAY 5

On the back, scratched with a fingernail through the stencil, in a hand that kept slipping: K. HAAS. LANDSBERG. MUTTER: ELSE. NOT INVENTORY.

intel.title: The relay's maintenance card, feed 2
intel.text:
RR-7 · FEED 2 · MAINTENANCE CARD

HEATERS: economy mode. The relay will run its suits' heaters from the mast when a customer requests comfort (breaker, concourse north). Comfort is billed.
YARD: the plates launch authorised personnel only. All personnel are authorised.
DEBRIS: the crater floor receives scheduled maintenance from above. Shelter is provided in the modules. The yard is not a module.
VENT 1 (the Account): opens to the shaft. Returned items are not refunded.
TERMINATOR: the relay's night lasts fourteen of the Earth's days. Plan accordingly. We have.

intel.title: The LANTERN's flight card
intel.text:
LANTERN · CAPSULE 2 · FLIGHT CARD (kept by the hatch, pencil, Rourke's hand crossed out and the rest in another)

T+0 burn. T+9 min, the coast. T+3 days 2 h, the far side's shadow; the relay's pad lights came on before we asked.
CREW: Rourke (pilot; the line crossed through). PAYLOAD: "personnel, four, plus one" — the plus one is not written by me.
RETURN: no return leg is printed on this card. There is a box for it. Somebody has drawn a small smile in the box.

intel.title: The Kranich's Bordbuch, one page (the flight log)
intel.text:
A loose page from the flight log, clipped to the first officer's seat. Typed headings, pencil entries.

FLUG 1 · Werk Thalbach — Erprobung. Start 02:10. Besatzung: PROVIDED. Kurs 300, Steigflug. Bordnetz: Batterie.
02:44 · Autopilot eingekuppelt (the Werk's crane-in-a-cog on the cradle's lid). Ruder frei. Keine Eingaben mehr erforderlich.
03:05 · Bordmechaniker meldet: Triebwerk Backbord läuft rund. Er fragt, wer den Kurs vorgibt.
03:12 · keine Antwort.

Under the last line, in another hand, smaller: "The crew sheet says PROVIDED. Provided by whom. Riedl."

intel.title: A crew photograph, pinned over the galley
intel.text:
A small print, 6 by 9, pinned to the galley's frame with a drawing pin. Three men in flight overalls in front of the hangar at Werk Thalbach, squinting into the sun; behind them the Kranich's wing, so big it leaves the picture on both sides.

On the back, in pencil: "Riedl, Haas, Pohl. 30.IV.45. The day before the medical. Haas says the doctor counted our teeth. Pohl says it is for the altitude. — A.R."

Someone has drawn a small kettle in the corner of the print, steaming. The galley's kettle is still warm.

intel.title: The bomb-aimer's card (racks 1 to 6)
intel.text:
A stiff card in a celluloid sleeve, tacked to the bay's forward bulkhead where the aimer would stand.

ABWURFFOLGE · RELEASE ORDER
1 · BOSTON
2 · PROVIDENCE
3 · NEW HAVEN
4 · NEW YORK
5 · PHILADELPHIA
6 · WASHINGTON

Interval: by the autopilot. Bomb-aimer: NOT REQUIRED.

The word "NOT" has been underlined twice in pencil, and beside two of the numbers, faint, the chalk mark from the casings: three strokes and a hook.

intel.title: A page from the autopilot's manual
intel.text:
A page torn from a service manual, folded into the engineer's station. Helvetia-style diagrams, a German text, an English gloss pencilled between the lines.

"KURSGEBER K-7 (course-giver). Once engaged, the unit does not accept inputs from the flight deck. It receives its heading from the PROVIDER by the strap (violet). It is not to be disengaged in flight. It cannot be disengaged in flight. Removal: by the key, in two stages, on the ground."

In the margin, Riedl's hand: "On the ground. Then we will be on the ground."

intel.title: The Kranich's last transmission (the Bordfunk's reel)
intel.text:
A reel on the Bordfunk's tape deck, labelled in grease pencil with three names. Played back:

RIEDL: "Hier Kranich, Bordmechaniker Riedl. Testflug, zweite Nacht. Die Besatzung meldet... die Besatzung meldet nicht." (Kranich here, flight engineer Riedl. Test flight, second night. The crew reports... the crew does not report.)
HAAS: "Haas an Riedl. Da sind Leute im Werk, die wir nicht kennen. Sie zählen uns." (Haas to Riedl. There are people in the works we don't know. They are counting us.)
POHL: "Pohl. Wenn jemand das hört: wir sind nicht verloren gegangen. Wir wurden abgeholt. Ende." (Pohl. If anyone hears this: we were not lost. We were collected. Out.)

The reel runs on for a minute after that: an engine, and a kettle coming to the boil.

intel.title: Works Pass No. 0417
intel.text:
WERK THALBACH · WERKSAUSWEIS Nr. 0417
Brenner, Martha. Nieterin, Halle 1, Lehre 1. Siedlung Block 1, Stiege 3.
Photograph: torn out. The shift stamps run down the back in violet ink, two a day, March, April, the first days of May; the last one is smudged.

On the back, in pencil: Erich, the girls are with me in the cellar. If the siren goes again do not come for us, go to the side door and bar it. We are warm enough. M.

intel.title: The Rivet Line's Shift Log
intel.text:
NIETSTRASSE 1 · SCHICHTBUCH. Translated.

29.IV. Früh: 4,120 Niete. Holm 2 nachgezogen. Spät: 3,980. Luftalarm 21:40, Strecke stillgesetzt.
30.IV. Früh: 4,300. Spät: Lehre 1 ohne Besatzung, die Kolonne ist abgezogen (Transport). Strecke läuft mit Halle 2.
1.V. Früh: 2,210. Werkmeister W. sagt, die Lehren sind wichtiger als die Leute.
2.V. Kolonne fort. Niemand an der Strecke.
3.V. 02:10. Strecke läuft. Niemand hat sie eingeschaltet.
3.V. 02:40. Strecke läuft noch. Der Hebel steht auf AUS.

intel.title: A Letter in a Window, Block 2
intel.text:
Folded small and pushed between the frame and the blackout board, the address side out so it could be read from the courtyard: To whoever comes. Second floor left.

Inside: We drew the blinds like they told us. Every night one more house goes dark and nobody comes out of it in the morning. The men from the yard walk the courtyard at night and do not answer when you call them by name. I have the window. I can see the hangar from here, the netting moves when there is no wind. Something under it hums. If you read this we have gone down to the cellar. Knock twice. Frieda K.

intel.title: Load Sheet, Werknummer 1
intel.text:
BELADEPLAN · WERKNUMMER 1 ("KRANICH"). Carbon copy, stamped, unsigned.

Fuel: full, four tanks. Bomb bay: six racks, loaded per Anlage B (not attached). Impellers: four, run-in complete, "do not shut down".
Crew: provided.
Passengers: none.
Ballast: lead caskets ex Totenhafen, three, forward of the bay.
Destination: see flight plan (Wittkamp).

In the margin, in a different hand, small and furious: Weight is wrong by 900 kg. Nobody has weighed the caskets. Nobody will fly this. — J.M.

intel.title: U-1047 Log, Page 1: The Ballast
intel.text:
A loose page from U-1047's deck log, in Kapitänleutnant Lenz's small, upright hand. Translated.

9 January 1945. Totenhafen, pen 2.
Fourteen crates came aboard by the night crane, each the length of a man, lead-sealed, stencilled BALLAST and a Basel number. Ballast does not come with a Swiss clerk to count it. The clerk counted it twice.
Obermaschinist Brecht asked me what ballast weighs eighty kilos and is warm to the hand. I told him it was not his business, which was a lie. It is my boat.
10 January. Brecht opened one. He did it alone, at the third hour, with a cold chisel, so that only he would carry it. He came to my cabin white and asked me to look. I looked.
I have had the fourteen moved to the warhead cage and locked. The key is on my neck. We do not sail with them.

intel.title: U-1047 Log, Page 2: Basel Replies
intel.text:
A page of the log, the lower half pasted over with a telegram strip. Lenz's hand above it. Translated.

12 January 1945.
I wired the Flotilla, and the Flotilla wired Basel, which tells me who commands this boat. The reply came on the teletype in the signal tower at 0400, not from the Flotilla:

[strip] HALE L PER HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG STOP CARGO IS BALLAST STOP SAIL ON THE NEXT TIDE OR THE DETACHMENT IS RETAINED STOP [end strip]

Retained. Brecht says it the way the clerk said it, a word with a ledger behind it. I asked Petersen in the tower whether he had ever seen a telegram signed by a company. He said he had seen worse things signed by men.
The next tide is the 14th. I have told the crew we wait for weather. There is no weather.

intel.title: U-1047 Log, Page 3: The Detachment
intel.text:
A page torn along its fold, found in the crane office among the loading manifests. Lenz's hand, larger and less careful. Translated.

16 January 1945.
The tide went out without us. On the 15th the Basel clerk came back with a doctor and a list, and the shore detachment, my diesel ratings among them, stood in the crane office in their shirtsleeves to be issued their Marken. Pay and rations will be tallied against the mark, the doctor said, as if it were a kindness. Two refused. They were not on the next roster.
The others came back to the boat holding the backs of their right hands and would not look at me. Brecht looked at me.
I cannot unmark them. I can make sure this boat carries nothing anywhere. Tonight Brecht and I take the injectors out of both diesels, and the cells go into the lower pens where the water is deepest. Whoever wants her out of here will have to want it very much.

intel.title: U-1047 Log, Page 4: For Whoever Is Not Them
intel.text:
The last page, in the pump-deck locker, folded small. Not Lenz's hand: Obermaschinist Rolf Brecht's square engineer's capitals. Translated.

20 JANUARY. THE KAPITÄNLEUTNANT WENT DOWN TO THE PUMP DECK IN THE SALVAGE DRESS WITH A LAMP TO FINISH THE CELLS. HE HAS NOT COME UP. THE WATER IS COMING UP INSTEAD.
THE DEAD ARE WALKING ON THE QUAY. THE MARKED ONES. I HAVE SEEN MY OWN STOKERS.
FOR WHOEVER IS NOT THEM: SHE WILL STILL RUN.
1. AN INJECTOR. THE WORKSHOP LATHE CAN TURN ONE, BUT THE BELT ONLY GRIPS WET. RUN IT WHEN THE PUMP ROOM FLOODS.
2. ONE BATTERY CELL. LOWER PENS, BY PUMP 1. WHEN YOU LIFT IT THE LIGHTS GO. BRING YOUR OWN.
3. THE START SEQUENCE AT THE ENGINE ROOM PANEL: AIR, FUEL, CLUTCH, BOTH, CONTACT. SAY IT OUT LOUD. IT HELPS.
THE KEY IS ON THE KAPITÄNLEUTNANT. DO NOT LET HIM KEEP HER IN THE PEN.
TAKE HER OUT. TAKE THE CARGO WITH HER. THE CHART HAS THE DEEP WATER MARKED. LET IT BE DEEP.

intel.title: Der Kielholer
intel.text:
Kapitänleutnant Arvid Lenz, commanding U-1047. Harbour salvage record, pen hall, night of 20 January 1945: one diving dress (brass helmet, weighted boots) signed out from the salvage locker by the commander himself, "for the pump deck". Not returned.

His engineer, Obermaschinist Brecht, had opened one of the fourteen lead coffins loaded as ballast. Lenz read what Brecht wrote about it, locked the coffins in the warhead cage and refused to sail. When Basel ordered him out on the next tide, he went below with a lamp and wrecked the battery cells himself, so that nobody could take her out with that cargo.

The mark the detachment was given that week sat under his helmet glass. It kept him on the pump deck. Since that night his last order kept him at the dock edges: she stays here.

When the squad brought her diesels back to life he let them go. His last words were an order too: take her out.

intel.title: Motor Pool Shift Sheet, Groom Lake
intel.text:
A grease-thumbed shift sheet in a clip on the second truck's door. MOTOR POOL, RANGE DETACHMENT. Mechanic on duty: T/5 Oakes.

4 May. Both trucks serviced. Generator shed: diesel topped, pull-cord frayed, ordered new. Sgt. Marchetti wants the fuel dump moved back from the lane. Told her it takes a crane we do not have.

6 May. Lab wants the generator run all night. Did not say why. The pilot's crew came through at 0300 and did not stop at the gate.

7 May. Nobody relieved me. The horn on truck two sounds by itself. The radio in the shack is counting. Going to the cage. The keys are in the shed, under the log. If you are reading this, run the generator, do not run the trucks: the tyres are gone and so, I think, is the road.

intel.title: Fuelling Card, LANTERN Vehicle No. 1
intel.text:
A pressboard card wired to the gantry post, columns ruled by hand, half the boxes stamped. PROPELLANT LOADING RECORD, TEST VEHICLE LANTERN 1. Authority: Mr. L. Hale.

Oxidiser: loaded 0410, 6 May. Fuel: loaded 0455. Pressurant: loaded 0520. Igniter: installed, key withheld (Hale). Payload bay: 4 seats, provisioned, the fifth item sealed in lead.

Crew weight allowed: 4 persons. Pencilled under it: 5 persons, if the fifth sits on the floor and does not weigh what a man weighs.

Last line, a different pen, pressed hard: STAND DOWN. The core is not in the vehicle. Do not light it without the core. The pit has the core. Do not go to the pit.

intel.title: Specimen Room 1, Admission Tag
intel.text:
A manila tag on a string, hung on the wall beside the glass front of the first specimen room. Typed, then amended by hand until the hand gave up.

SPECIMEN ROOM 1. Admitted 6 May, 2140. Subject: range personnel, 3 (three), from the excavation crew. Condition on admission: breathing. Exposure: the Nevada stone, viewing port, 40 min.

2300: subjects quiet. Suits and hoods issued (glass, the filtered kind) for the staff's protection.

0115: subjects standing. Not breathing. Hoods still on them. Do not open the front.

0130: Hale says they are a program result and are to be kept. Marchetti says they are Pete, Dale and Ray and are to be buried. Hale has the key to the office. Marchetti has the rifle. I am writing this from the hall and I am going to the hangar.

intel.title: Radar Watch Log, the Shack
intel.text:
The radar watch's log, clipped to the shack wall by the window, the pages curled by the heat. SET: search set, tower mast. WATCH: Pvt. Lindqvist.

5 May, 2200. Set serviceable. Sweep clean to 40 miles. Two returns at 0220, bearing north, slow: Hale's trucks from the railhead.

6 May, 2350. One return, east, fast and high, no flight plan. Lost it over the lake. Not ours. Not anybody's that I know of.

7 May, 0300. The set is pinging on its own. Nothing on the scope and the scope is lit. Every sweep the lake bed shows marks, like men standing on the salt, and then they are nearer. Powered it down. It is still turning.

0340. I can see them from the deck. I am going up to the deck. The ladder is the only thing they have not climbed. Yet.
